turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the LARGEST SHG
tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

## Key patterns from training data

Looking at the highest SHG values in training:
- **Te-based tetrahedral chalcopyrites**: Tl8Te12 (239), Zn2Ga4Te8 (92), Cd2Ga4Te8 (92), Li2In4Cu2Te8 (74), Ga4Hg2Se8 (73)
- **Non-centrosymmetric tellurides/selenides with polar chains**: Ge/Te/Pb/Se (302!), Zn4Sn4P8 (84), Mg4Ge4As8 (122)
- **Ternary Se chalcopyrites (I-III-VI2 type)**: Ga2Cu2Ge2Se8 (54), Ga2Ag2Sn2Se8 (54), In2Cu2Ge2Se8 (46), Al2Cu2Sn2Se8 (49)

The strongest drivers: **heavy chalcogens (Te > Se > S)**, tetrahedral non-centrosymmetric frameworks, and polarizable cations (Cu, Ag, Hg, In).

## Screening the pool

**Al4Hg2Se8 (c082)**: Direct analog of training Ga4Hg2Se8 (SHG = 72.7) and Al4Hg2S8 (21.1). Al-Hg-Se tetrahedral defect-chalcopyrite → very high. Strong candidate.

**Al2Cu2Ge2Se8 (c071)**: Analog of Ga2Cu2Ge2Se8 (54.5), Al2Cu2Sn2Se8 (49.2). Chalcopyrite Se → high.

**In2Ag2Ge2Se8 (c056)**: Analog of In2Ag2/Cu2 Se8 chalcopyrites (~46–60). In2Ag2Sn2Se8 in training = 59.6. High.

**Al4Cu4Se8 (c093)**: Analog of Al-Cu-Se tetrahedral; Cu selenides tend to be high (~50).

**Mg-Ga-Se family (c001–c004, c031–c036)**: LiMgGaSe/MgGaSe4 training values ~3–62; variable. c095 (Li2MgGa2Se5) type shows moderate values. Not top tier.

**Cd1In3Te4As1 (c073)**: Telluride, non-centrosymmetric, heavy polarizable atoms → likely very high, comparable to Te chalcopyrites (>50).

**Zn3Cu6As4S12 (c047)**: sulfide, moderate.

Prioritizing Te-containing and Se-chalcopyrites with polarizable cations:

- c073 (In-Te-As, telluride) — heaviest, likely highest
- c082 (Al4Hg2Se8) — direct high analog
- c056 (In2Ag2Ge2Se8) — chalcopyrite Se
- c071 (Al2Cu2Ge2Se8) — chalcopyrite Se
- c093 (Al4Cu4Se8) — Cu selenide tetrahedral

Final: c073, c082, c056, c071, c093
